Problem Statement
Explain the problem and why it matters.

Traditional web browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) were built purely for manual human consumption. As AI assistants evolved, integrating automation required clunky browser extensions, third-party API copy-pasting, or external scripts.

runs.text: Traditional web browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) were built purely for manual human consumption. As AI assistants evolved, integrating automation required clunky browser extensions, third-party API copy-pasting, or external scripts.

paragraphs.text: Existing "AI Browsers" or AI automation frameworks suffer from critical drawbacks:

runs.text: Existing "AI Browsers" or AI automation frameworks suffer from critical drawbacks:

paragraphs.text: Cloud Lock-in & Privacy Risks: Most AI tools force users to send all browsing data, credentials, and DOM contents to closed-source third-party cloud APIs.

runs.text: : Most AI tools force users to send all browsing data, credentials, and DOM contents to closed-source third-party cloud APIs.

paragraphs.text: Lack of Local Model Support: Users cannot run AI agents offline or use self-hosted open-source models (like Ollama, Llama 3, Qwen, or Mistral) for private tasks.

, Llama 3, Qwen, or Mistral) for private tasks.

paragraphs.text: DOM Bloat & High Latency: Modern web pages contain megabytes of scripts, ads, and trackers, which bloat the LLM context window, causing 45s+ delays per step and high API token costs.

runs.text: : Modern web pages contain megabytes of scripts, ads, and trackers, which bloat the LLM context window, causing 45s+ delays per step and high API token costs.

paragraphs.text: Flaky Browser Control: Existing CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) integrations frequently crash or fail on socket connection timeouts (WSAEWOULDBLOCK / port 9222 locked) on desktop OS environments.

paragraphs.text: PROPOSED SOLUTION:
Describe the idea and how it solves the problem
Pluto Agent Browser is an open-source, AI-native desktop Chromium browser built from the ground up to unite human browsing and autonomous AI agent execution in a single application.

runs.text: is an open-source, AI-native desktop Chromium browser built from the ground up to unite human browsing and autonomous AI agent execution in a single application.

paragraphs.text: Pluto connects a multi-tab Electron desktop shell with a local Python FastAPI backend powered by an optimized browser-use CDP controller.

runs.text: powered by an optimized browser-use CDP controller.

Local & Cloud LLM Freedom: Native out-of-the-box support for local models via Ollama, as well as high-speed cloud models (ChatBrowserUse, Gemini, Claude, GPT-4o).

paragraphs.text: Built-in Adblocking & DOM Pruning: Integrated Ghostery/uBlock engine strips trackers and ads before sending page data to the LLM, reducing token cost by over 60%.

paragraphs.text: Idea/Approach
Mention the tools and technologies to be used with a brief description.
Pluto solves the fundamental problem of agent-browser communication by making the desktop browser shell itself aware of the agent backend.

runs.text: Pluto solves the fundamental problem of agent-browser communication by making the desktop browser shell itself aware of the agent backend.

paragraphs.text: Dual-Tab Synchronous Rendering: When an agent executes a task, it doesn't open a hidden headless instance; it attaches directly to Electron BrowserView tabs via CDP.

paragraphs.text: Context-Optimized Token Pruning: Instead of sending the full DOM history on every turn, Pluto trims history down to $O(1)$ step windows (max_history_items=6) and compresses screenshots, achieving 4× reduction in token payload size.

paragraphs.text: Dynamic Socket Isolation: Electron dynamically checks and assigns available CDP ports (9222, 9223, 9224...) at startup, passing environment variables down to the backend process to eliminate socket conflicts.
